# SSAC27 full paper — decision value of translation (E7, E8, E9): RESULTS

**Generated by `scripts/render_sloan_fullpaper_decisions_note.py` from the outputs of `scripts/sloan_fullpaper_decisions.py` (retained run `decide-02`), committed under `docs/research/artifacts/sloan-fullpaper-decisions-2026-11-03/`. Every number below is read from those files.** Pre-registration: `docs/research/sloan-full-paper-preregistration-2026-11-03.md` (commit `f52e7c831`), sections E7, E8 and E9.

**EXPLORATORY.** Destination seasons 2020–2025 were inspected for the submitted abstract, so nothing here is a confirmatory test. Only P1 (2026-27) is confirmatory, and no 2026-27 statistic was read: the box-score loader read seasons 2020–2025 only.

## In plain words

* **Primary (D2).** Adding translation to the league-aware model changes 2.6% of head-to-head comparisons (95% CI 2.0-3.1%) and is right on 54.4% of those (95% CI 46.0-63.9%), which is not distinguishable from a coin flip; the smallest departure from 50% this test could detect with 80% power is about 13.0 percentage points.
* For comparison, adding translation to a history-only forecast changes 6.9% of comparisons (95% CI [5.7, 7.9]%) and is right on 57.3% of those (95% CI [50.8, 63.2]%). Translation moves rankings when the forecast does not know the leagues; once it knows them, it moves very few.
* **Ordering (D1).** All four forecasts put the better player first in about 72%–74% of within-pool pairs. The league-aware model without translation orders 0.17 percentage points more of the pairs correctly than history + translation (95% CI [-0.43, 0.79]).
* **Intervals (E8).** Walk-forward conformal intervals for the league-aware model cover close to their nominal level (both pooled coverage intervals include it): 80% intervals cover 82.6% and 95% intervals cover 95.2% of 2021–2025 newcomers, at a width of about ±4.8 and ±7.4 EFF/36. By season, 80% coverage ranges 74.0%–90.4%.
* **League table (E9).** The ten source leagues fall into 3 tiers. Leagues inside a tier cannot be told apart and must not be ranked against each other.

## Forecast error on one scale (context)

| Model | MAE (EFF/36) | D1 ordering accuracy | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| history | 3.096 | 72.1% | [70.1, 74.2]% |
| history + translation | 2.935 | 73.1% | [71.0, 75.2]% |
| offsets λ10 | 2.924 | 73.3% | [71.4, 75.3]% |
| offsets λ10 + translation | 2.926 | 73.5% | [71.5, 75.6]% |

Adding translation to history lowers MAE by 5.2% of the history model's MAE (3.096 → 2.935). Adding it to the league-aware model raises MAE by 0.1% of that model's MAE (2.924 → 2.926); the submitted abstract's interval for this increment spans zero.

### D1: pairwise ordering accuracy

| Contrast (positive favours the second) | Accuracy difference | 95% CI (points) | 80%-power detectable difference | Read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| history + translation → offsets λ10 | 0.17 pts | [-0.43, 0.79] | 0.85 pts | spans zero |
| offsets λ10 → offsets λ10 + translation | 0.22 pts | [-0.21, 0.71] | 0.66 pts | spans zero |

**Reference (split-half, from per-game box scores).**

| Reading | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Split-half pairwise agreement, odd vs even appearances (pre-registered) | 68.8% [0.662, 0.712] | each half ≈ 8.9 games |
| Split-half correlation of EFF/36 (within pool) | 0.517 | Spearman-Brown full-season reliability 0.682 |
| Normal-model check of the split-half agreement | 67.3% | should sit near the measured agreement |
| Full-season bound: true rate vs full-season outcome (normal model; supplementary, not pre-registered) | 80.9% | what a forecaster who knew each player's true rate would reach |

**Read this carefully.** The pre-registered split-half agreement (68.8%) is *below* every model's D1 (72.1%–73.5%). It is not an upper bound: both halves carry half-season noise, whereas the models are scored against the full season. The full-season bound (80.9%) is the meaningful ceiling. Of the ordering accuracy reachable above chance (50%) under that bound, the models reach history 72%, history + translation 75%, offsets λ10 75%, offsets λ10 + translation 76%.

How to read it. Leagues in the same tier are **not distinguishable**: adjacent leagues inside a tier must not be ranked. The rule compares each league with the top league of its tier, not with every league in the tier above, so a league at the top of one tier may also not be distinguishable from the bottom of the tier above. The tiers are identical for both destinations, because the model's league offset does not depend on the destination; only the level shifts.

Tier boundaries near the line (share within 0.05 of the 0.90 rule, so a small change in data could move them): italy-lba 0.884 (tier 1); israel-bsl 0.864 (tier 2); aba-league 0.942 (tier 3).

The club-ready version is `docs/research/artifacts/sloan-fullpaper-decisions-2026-11-03/e9_league_tiers_club.csv` (one row per league × destination, with a how-to-read column).

## Against the submitted abstract

No contradiction. The abstract says translation adds nothing detectable once the forecast knows the leagues. In decision terms the same holds: few comparisons change and the changed ones are not distinguishable from a coin flip; the ordering-accuracy gain spans zero.

## What this licenses

* The D2 sentence, exactly: *Adding translation to the league-aware model changes 2.6% of head-to-head comparisons (95% CI 2.0-3.1%) and is right on 54.4% of those (95% CI 46.0-63.9%), which is not distinguishable from a coin flip; the smallest departure from 50% this test could detect with 80% power is about 13.0 percentage points.*
* E8: "walk-forward conformal intervals for the recommended model cover close to their nominal level" with the coverage numbers above; descriptive only.
* E9: the tier table, as tiers; never a rank order inside a tier.
* Not licensed: any confirmatory claim (all of this is exploratory), any ranking inside a tier, or reading the split-half agreement as a ceiling.
